p: With two big universities in the city, Nottingham has a huge student population, and karting has become a popular choice for societies, birthdays and end-of-term celebrations. It's competitive, it's social, and it's a good laugh whether you're a petrolhead or have never driven before.

For student groups, a bit of planning helps. Book well ahead around the end of term, when lots of societies have the same idea. Collect money in advance to save awkward chats on the day, and give everyone a meeting time that's earlier than the race slot.

First-timers should focus on staying smooth. Look ahead through the bends, brake before you turn and ease back on the power as the kart straightens up. Don't worry if the first few laps are slow; everyone gets quicker as they go.
The city's trams also make it easy for students to get about without a car, linking the centre with the universities and the suburbs.

Nottingham has plenty more to fill a day. The National Justice Museum, in the old Shire Hall in the Lace Market, lets you explore centuries of crime and punishment, complete with courtrooms and cells. Green's Windmill in Sneinton is a working windmill and science centre that once belonged to mathematician George Green. And for a breather, the Arboretum is a lovely Victorian park close to the city centre.
